name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia limits; Zaporizhzhia outage 8 Nov
summary: New START lapsed without replacement; Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power on 8 Nov; no nuclear test or alert change found
state: New START expired on 5 Feb 2026 with no replacement agreement described (Carnegie). The Zaporizhzhia plant lost all off-site power on 8 Nov and switched to emergency diesel generators, with fuel for about two weeks; IAEA head Rafael Grossi called the safety situation precarious (Anadolu), and power was restored hours later (Reuters via Yahoo). Searches on 9 Nov found no nuclear test, change in alert levels or new explicit threat of use.
for_you: Reports of the 8 Nov outage described no radiation release. The IAEA publishes Zaporizhzhia updates, and national radiation-protection agencies are the official source if advice is ever issued.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START, expired 5 Feb 2026); no nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use found

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
